0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Anjou is not just the kingdom of Chenin Blanc; it also offers one of the richest spectrums of rosé in France. From the sweet Cabernet-d'Anjou, to the neutral, easy-drinking Rosé-d'Anjou, to the dry and refined Rosé-de-Loire, and to Haut-Poitou on the southern plateau — this lesson takes you through every facet of Anjou's rosé world.

Learning Objectives

🌹 Tell apart the sweetness of Anjou's three rosé AOCs

Master the varieties, styles and residual-sugar rules of Cabernet-d'Anjou, Rosé-d'Anjou and Rosé-de-Loire

🍇 Know Grolleau, a local variety

Learn how Grolleau (Groslot), planted almost only in Anjou, produces large volumes of easy-drinking rosé

🏔️ Explore the plateau character of Haut-Poitou

Learn how the southern plateau region became its own AOC in 2011, and the character of its whites and reds
1.title: The Sweetness Spectrum of Anjou Rosés
1.highlights.0.title: Cabernet-d'Anjou (off-dry)
1.highlights.0.content: Cabernet Franc + Cabernet Sauvignon, legal residual sugar 10–40 g/L, elegantly floral, one of France's best-selling sweet rosé AOCs
1.highlights.1.title: Rosé-d'Anjou (off-dry)
1.highlights.1.content: Mainly Grolleau, with Cabernet and Gamay permitted, residual sugar about 7–30 g/L, slightly less sweet than Cabernet-d'Anjou, sweet and easy-drinking, for drinking young
1.highlights.2.title: Rosé-de-Loire (dry)
1.highlights.2.content: Dry rosé, Cabernet Franc-led (at least 30%), residual sugar ≤ 3 g/L, the most serious and refined of the three rosés
1.content:
Anjou's three rosé AOCs represent three very different stylistic orientations, with the key differences in grape variety and residual sugar:

AOCMain varietiesResidual sugarStyle
Cabernet-d'AnjouCab. Franc + Cab. Sauv.10–40 g/L (off-dry)Floral, raspberry, violet, elegant finish
Rosé-d'AnjouGrolleau-led7–30 g/L (off-dry)Strawberry, peach, sweet and easy-drinking, an everyday table wine
Rosé-de-LoireCab. Franc ≥30%≤ 3 g/L (dry)Crisp, mineral, red fruit, versatile with food

Pairing suggestions: Cabernet-d'Anjou with light desserts; Rosé-de-Loire with summer grilled seafood or salmon dishes.
2.title: Grolleau — Anjou's Own Local Hero
2.content:
Grolleau (also spelled Groslot) is an old variety planted almost only in Anjou and hardly found elsewhere in France. It is not a "great variety," but it is the backbone of Anjou's rosé culture.

🌱 Viticultural traits

High yielding, early ripening, easy to grow. Grows well on Anjou's schist and clay soils.

🍷 In the winery

Pale colour, medium acidity, low tannin, naturally sweet (high sugar). Very suited to pale, sweet rosés.

🗺️ Planting area

Concentrated mainly within the Anjou and Rosé-d'Anjou AOCs, with lower proportions allowed in Cabernet-d'Anjou and Rosé-de-Loire.

Grolleau represents a culture of "everyday consumption" — not seeking complexity, only freshness and pleasure. The cool rosé that locals drink in summer is often the sweet figure of Rosé-d'Anjou.
3.title: Haut-Poitou — An Independent Newcomer on the Plateau
3.content:
Haut-Poitou lies south of Anjou, on the plateau north of Poitiers. In 2011 it was promoted from VDQS to a full AOC, making it one of the most important southernmost regions of the Loire basin.

🏔️ Geography and climate

A limestone plateau, higher than the Anjou plain, with a more continental climate, hot summers and cold winters; large day–night temperature swings help retain acidity.

🍇 Main varieties

White: Sauvignon Blanc (main), Chardonnay (secondary). Red: Cabernet Franc, a little Gamay.

🍷 Style character

Sauvignon Blanc is crisper and tighter than Touraine's, with high acidity, herbal and white-flower aromas and occasionally flinty minerality, a very good-value Loire white.

Haut-Poitou is a small surprise on the Loire's southern flank — not widely known, but its Sauvignon Blanc often recalls the crisp mineral style of Pouilly-Fumé at one-third of the price.
4.title: Quiz
4.questions.0.question: What is the biggest difference between Cabernet-d'Anjou and Rosé-de-Loire?
4.questions.0.options.0: They use completely different grape varieties
4.questions.0.options.1: Cabernet-d'Anjou is off-dry (10–40 g/L residual sugar), Rosé-de-Loire is dry (≤3 g/L)
4.questions.0.options.2: Both are dry, differing only in depth of colour
4.questions.0.options.3: Rosé-de-Loire is made only outside Anjou
4.questions.0.explanation: The key difference between the two is residual sugar: Cabernet-d'Anjou has a legal residual sugar of 10–40 g/L (off-dry), while Rosé-de-Loire is legally dry (residual sugar ≤ 3 g/L). Both use Cabernet Franc as an important variety, but with different proportion requirements.
4.questions.1.question: What is Grolleau's main viticultural characteristic?
4.questions.1.options.0: Low yield, late ripening, high acidity, suited to sweet wines
4.questions.1.options.1: High yield, early ripening, naturally high sugar, very suited to pale, sweet rosés
4.questions.1.options.2: Can only grow in the cool north
4.questions.1.options.3: A genetic mutation of Cabernet Franc
4.questions.1.explanation: Grolleau's high yield and naturally high sugar make it the first-choice variety for Anjou's large-volume production of sweet rosé (Rosé-d'Anjou); planted almost only in Anjou, it is a unique local agricultural heritage.
